name: Loic Pix - playable portfolio
studio: Loic Picon (Loic Pix, one-man animation studio)
stack: three.js r180 (REVISION "180" in the shipped three.module chunk)
Blender (baked animation exported as GLB under /blender/bakes/)
techniques: portfolio staged as a playable arcade run instead of a project grid
Blender-baked animation shipped as one GLB spanning frames 0000-1185 (/blender/bakes/pix_experience_0000_1185.glb)
meshopt-compressed mobile variants of the scene, floor and character GLBs
SkinnedMesh character with morph targets and an atlas-textured deform rig
shader patches through onBeforeCompile
Web Audio rhythm transport at 138 BPM driving combo, multiplier and PERFECT timing
skills presented as a 13-item CREATIVE LOADOUT and software as EQUIPPED items
public high-score board with an optional, explicitly unverified Instagram handle
pixel ratio adapted at runtime from measured performance, clamped between 0.5 and 1.25
Quality / Performance toggle on the loader ('Older computer? Choose Performance.')
rotate-your-phone gate and a STOP control for the whole experience
binary intro sequence with its own loading atlas (/ui/gauntlet-intro/sequence.bin)
palette: near-black #050505 ground with a warm gold ramp #ffe44f / #ffba16 / #f58b09 / #ca6900, deep navy #151c2d and cream #fffdf2, read from the served HTML; the 1440 render of the loader shows a gold-rimmed orange character in a teal glow on black
type: Oxanium, self-hosted as 'Pix Oxanium' (variable, weight 200-800) for the interface; 'Secret Power', a pixel display face, for titles and counters - the loader percentage renders in blocky pixel digits
motion: loader: the character turns in a glow over a pixel-digit percentage counter; the experience runs on a 138 BPM rhythm lane with combos, a SCROLL TO ASSEMBLE step, drag-and-drop side quests and a MISSION COMPLETE score card. prefers-reduced-motion removes the CSS transitions on the stop control and the legal link; whether the 3D run itself changes under reduced motion was not observed.
why: On the threejs.org homepage showcase, posted by @threejs on 16 September 2026 (https://x.com/threejs/status/2100224277064904830) quoting the author's post: 'THIS IS NOT A VIDEO. THIS IS MY PLAYABLE PORTFOLIO. I could've made a normal portfolio. But I'm me. So I turned every idea in my head into one playable web experience.' (https://x.com/LoicPix/status/2100209698204950760, tagged @Blender @threejs). The transferable idea: the portfolio is the proof - an animator demonstrates animation, timing and character work with a rhythm-timed piece instead of listing them, and the CV survives as game UI (a loadout of skills, equipped software, a high-score table). Caveat worth knowing before copying it: the served HTML still carries placeholder rows ('PROJECT TITLE / VIDEO / IMAGE / LINK') under SELECTED WORK and a shipped debug panel (ANIMATION LANES, GANT DEBUG); whether the runtime fills or hides them was not observed. Verified from the live HTML, both CSS files, the entry and viewer chunks, and a UFS look render at 1440 (loader only).

name: Rainy Worlds
stack: three.js WebGPURenderer (three/webgpu), with a forceWebGL fallback
TSL node materials and GPU compute (computeAsync, instancedArray)
techniques: six walkable worlds behind one menu: Exploring Woods, The Headland, Night Drive, The Canyon, Wheat Field, The Pass
three ways to move through the rain: walk and run, pedal a bike, drive a car
car interior controls: wipers (E), headlights (H), radio (R)
rain and wind intensity on keys 1-4
Y opens a dialog: paste a YouTube link and it plays under the rain
WebGPU adapter asked for up to 32 sampled textures per shader stage, falling back to WebGL through forceWebGL
TSL post chain: TAA with a 0.14 sharpen, bloom, quality-tiered motion blur (6 or 8 samples), saturation 1.58 and contrast 1.13 grade, vignette 0.28, grain 0.022, chromatic aberration 0.006
range and density fog
LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH quality chooser and a backend note on the start card
pointer-lock mouse look
'Best experienced with headphones'
palette: cold wet greys: ground #0b0d0f, text #cfd6dc, overlay rgba(6,8,10,.78), greys #a5b2b6 / #819398 / #98a6ab, warm accents #e9b9ad / #ffd9c2 - all read from the served HTML
type: ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace for the whole interface; the h1 is weight 300 at 30px with .42em tracking, buttons carry .22em tracking in capitals; Georgia, serif is also declared in the page CSS
motion: the start overlay fades out over 0.8s into a first-person wander; the rain scene itself was not observed here - the UFS look render timed out on this WebGPU page in headless Chrome
why: On the threejs.org homepage showcase, posted by @threejs on 6 September 2026 (https://x.com/threejs/status/2096467352783356011) quoting the author's post: 'Rainy Worlds is live. Six rainy worlds you can wander in your browser, built with @threejs WebGPU. Press Y, paste a song, walk in the rain. Made for Pluviophiles: the one who is happiest when it pours.' (https://x.com/mkcuriosity/status/2096244054556057918). The transferable idea: hold one feeling constant (rain) across six places and three ways of moving instead of stuffing one world with features, and let the visitor bring the soundtrack - a one-field feature that turns a rendering demo into something personal. The grade lives as named, tunable renderer uniforms (vignette, grain, CA, saturation, contrast, sharpen), a clean shape for a TSL post chain. The page now also offers an 'Act 1' story mode ('Your sister is missing. Follow what she left behind.'). Verified from the served HTML and the Vite bundle; not visually rendered.

name: Jelly Baby
studio: Scott Sun (@scottstts), built with GPT-6 Astra (Codex) per the author's post and the repo's .codex/AGENTS.md
stack: WebGPU only - the r185 WebGL fallback is explicitly disabled
a Web Worker for the optical transport
techniques: XPBD soft body: a 980-node tetrahedral cage with 4,026 elements, 1/240 s fixed step, 3 iterations
72,234-vertex visible surface embedded in the cage by barycentric weights, not a canned squash-and-stretch pose
grab, stretch and throw the character through a force-limited grab constraint
GPU caustic field plus a worker-computed thickness and shadow field from a 10,090-vertex optical proxy
AgX tone mapping at exposure 1.05 with sRGB output
drawing buffer capped at four million pixels: dpr = min(devicePixelRatio, 1.7, sqrt(4e6 / (w * h)))
compileAsync warmup with visibility and frustum culling disabled so no pipeline compiles mid-play
80 physics settle steps before the first frame is shown
day and night HDR environments preloaded as RGBA16F
four flavours (lime, strawberry, blueberry, lemon) as a palette picker
facilities: swing, trampoline, bed, tricycle, soccer, portal worlds
touch joystick and hop button; sound starts on the first interaction and can be muted
palette: warm studio cream: theme and ground #e8d9c3, loader #eee7d9, olive ink #394028, sage #799342, joystick knob #b8cf8d, frosted panels #f7f3e7 at 30-85% alpha; the jelly is lime by default
type: Georgia italic for the display lines ('A little life.' - h1 44px, -2.4px tracking; loader h2 39px), a ui-sans-serif system stack for the interface, 9px sans key caps
motion: the wobble is simulated, not keyframed - gravity is a deliberately low 2.4 m/s2 so the elastic response has time to show; the loader fades over .7s; prefers-reduced-motion stops the loader mark's animation and the transitions
why: On the threejs.org homepage showcase, posted by @threejs on 6 September 2026 (https://x.com/threejs/status/2096433465755369854) quoting the author's post: 'People seem to love the bouncy jelly, so I made this Jelly Baby game with Astra in @threejs' (https://x.com/scottstts/status/2096364764054131119). An agent-built exhibit like Whiteout, but documented: every number above is stated in the repo's own docs. The transferable idea: simulate the one property the thing is about - softness - and spend the budget there; a 7 cm character on a tabletop with no score and no errands, with the physics tuned for feel (gentle gravity) over realism. Worth copying on any 3D page: warm every pipeline and settle the physics behind the loader so the first visible frame is already stable. WebGPU-only, so the headless render stopped at the loader ('A little life. Loading the little room'). Verified from the source (README, docs/architecture.md, docs/soft-body-and-interaction.md, docs/rendering-and-materials.md, src/style.css, index.html, package.json) and a UFS look render at 1440.
